{{Navbar-Global_Coal_Plant_Tracker}}
'''Jimah East power station''' is an operating power station of at least 2000-megawatts (MW) in Port Dickson, Negeri Sembilan, Malaysia.
It is also known as Tuanku Muhriz Power Station, Project 3B.

==Ownership Tree==

This ownership tree is part of the [https://globalenergymonitor.org/projects/global-energy-ownership-tracker/ Global Energy Ownership Tracker], a project of Global Energy Monitor.

{{#widget:ObservableOwnershipTree|}}

==Background==

In April 2013, the Energy Commission (EC) shortlisted five consortia to tender for the 2,000 MW Project 3B coal-fired power plant, to be developed at the respective consortium's proposed site. The five shortlisted consortia were 1Malaysia Development Bhd (1MDB), Formis Resources Bhd, Tenaga Nasional Bhd (TNB), Malakoff Corp Bhd and YTL Power International Bhd. 1MDB had proposed the plant to be located at Jimah, Negri Sembilan, while Malakoff had proposed Pulau Carey, Selangor. Both Formis and YTL Power had proposed Tanjung Tohor, Johor. TNB had proposed Tanjung Hantu - Segari, Perak.<ref>[http://www.thestar.com.my/Business/Business-News/2013/04/19/Energy-Commission-shortlists-5-for-2000MW-power-plant/ "Energy Commission shortlists 5 for 2,000MW power plant,"] The Star, April 19, 2013</ref> 

In March 2013, it was announced that 1Malaysia Development Bhd and partner Mitsui Co Ltd had been selected to build the project, offering a levelised tariff of 25.33 sen a kWh. The project would use IHI ultra-supercritical technology steam generator and two units of Toshiba turbo generator.<ref name="sun">[http://www.thesundaily.my/news/973005 "IMDB clinch Project 3B coal fired plant,"] The Sun Daily, March 3, 2014</ref> The plant would be built in Mukim Jimah, Port Dickson, Negeri Sembilan near the existing Jimah power station.<ref name="sun">[http://www.thesundaily.my/news/973005 "IMDB clinch Project 3B coal fired plant,"] The Sun Daily, March 3, 2014</ref><ref name="intense">Gurmeet Kaur, [http://bit.ly/1cm703Z "Intense lobbying has stalled decision-making for the 2,000MW coal-fired power plant under Project 3B,"] The Star Online, February 8, 2014</ref> 

The selection followed an intense period of lobbying for the project by the two front runners, YTL Power and 1MDB.<ref name="intense">Gurmeet Kaur, [http://bit.ly/1cm703Z "Intense lobbying has stalled decision-making for the 2,000MW coal-fired power plant under Project 3B,"] The Star Online, February 8, 2014</ref>

In February 2015, 1MDB said it expected to withdraw from the 3B power project due to lack of funding, thereby allowing Malaysia's largest power group Tenaga Nasional Bhd (TNB) to take over the project.<ref>[http://www.reuters.com/article/2015/02/07/malaysia-sukuk-1mdb-idUSL6N0VG2HT20150207 "Malaysia's 1MDB calls off $2.4 bln sukuk for power project-sources,"] Reuters, February 7, 2015</ref> Due to the transfer, Project 3B was postponed from the originally proposed October 2018 start date to June 2019.<ref>[http://www.thestar.com.my/Business/Business-News/2015/06/30/Project-3B-plant-operation-date-postponed/?style=biz "Project 3B plant ops date delayed due to transfer from 1MDB to TNB,"] The Star, June 30, 2015</ref>

In August 2016, it was reported that construction had begun on the project.<ref>[http://asian-power.com/ipp/news/construction-kicks-off-rm12b-jimah-east-power-project-in-malaysia "Construction kicks off on RM12b Jimah East Power Project in Malaysia,"] Asia Power, August 2, 2016</ref>

In March 2017, it was reported the plant was on-track for completion in December 2019.<ref>[http://www.thestar.com.my/business/business-news/2017/03/27/tnbs-jimah-project-on-track-for-completion-by-december-2019/ "TNB's Jimah project on track for completion by December 2019,"] The Star, March 27, 2017</ref>

Construction was 75% complete as of April 2018.<ref>[https://themalaysianreserve.com/2018/04/04/tnb-completes-75-of-works-in-jimah-east-power-plant/ TNB completes 75% of works in Jimah East Power plant], The Malaysian Reserve, April 4, 2018</ref>

In May 2019, it was reported that Unit 1 would be commissioned in June 2019, and Unit 2 would be commissioned in December 2019.<ref>[https://www.bharian.com.my/bisnes/korporat/2019/05/563833/tnb-peruntuk-perbelanjaan-modal-lebih-rendah TNB peruntuk perbelanjaan modal lebih rendah], BH Online, May 14, 2019</ref>

Unit 1 was commissioned on August 21, 2019.<ref>Chong Jin Hun, [https://www.theedgemarkets.com/article/tnb-jimah-easts-first-power-plant-starts-commercial-operations "TNB Jimah East's First Power Plant Starts Commercial Operations,"] The Edge Markets, August 22, 2019</ref> Unit 2 was commissioned on December 27, 2019.<ref>[https://themalaysianreserve.com/2019/12/31/tnbs-jimah-east-power-plant-now-fully-operational/ TNB’s Jimah East Power plant now fully operational], The Malaysian Reserve, December 31, 2019</ref>

According to an August 2025 report, a "major overhaul" of Unit 2 was planned for May 2026.<ref>[https://www.midf.com.my/sites/corporate/files/2025-08/tnb-vn-jimah_east_power-mbsbr-260825.pdf Visit Note: Jimah East Power], MBSB Investment Bank, August 26, 2025</ref>

==Planned Retirement==

In August 2022, TNB announced that they would be retiring selected coal plants earlier than planned and would be replacing the generation with renewable energy alternatives. The President and CEO of the firm stated: "TNB is very much in the driver’s seat when it comes to delivering the nation’s energy transition, and this responsibility is the impetus for TNB to accelerate our ESG initiatives". Subject to approval, the power stations initially targeted for early retirement were Jimah East power station, [[Sultan Aziz power station]] and [[Manjung power station]].<ref>[https://themalaysianreserve.com/2022/08/02/tnb-to-retire-selected-coal-plants-earlier-than-scheduled/ TNB to retire selected coal plants earlier than scheduled], The Malaysian Reserve, August 2, 2022</ref>

In May 2023, it was reported that TNB had committed to retiring the coal plant in 2044.<ref name=cofirehm23>[https://themalaysianreserve.com/2023/05/31/malaysias-potential-in-re-transition/ Malaysia’s potential in RE transition], The Malaysian Reserve, May 31, 2023</ref>

In December 2025, TNB reiterated that all of its coal plants would be retired by 2045.<ref name=dec25>[https://www.tnb.com.my/assets/annual_report/TNB_IAR2025_Sustainability_Statement.pdf TNB Sustainability Statement 2025], Tenaga Nasional Bhd, December 31, 2025</ref>

===Possible emissions reduction technologies in the plant's future===
A May 2023 news article reported that feasibility studies were underway to assess options for co-firing ammonia and biomass with coal at the power plant.<ref name=cofirehm23>[https://themalaysianreserve.com/2023/05/31/malaysias-potential-in-re-transition/ Malaysia’s potential in RE transition], The Malaysian Reserve, May 31, 2023</ref>

In October 2023, co-firing feasibility studies for hydrogen, ammonia, and biomass were "ongoing".<ref>[https://www.thestar.com.my/business/business-news/2023/10/26/tnb-quickens-move-into-renewable-energy TNB quickens move into renewable energy], The Star, October 26, 2023</ref>

In June 2024, a carbon capture and utilization project, called "Project Dragon", was initiated at Jimah East power station.<ref>[https://www.tnb.com.my/sustainability/esg-stories-urgency-of-carbon-emission-management Calling for Action: The Urgency of Carbon Emission Management for a Sustainable Future], Tenaga Nasional Bhd, September 26, 2024</ref>

In April 2025, TNB's 2024 Annual Report stated that the demonstration carbon capture unit at Jimah East power station was 30% complete. The report also stated that a pilot ammonia co-firing demonstration was "gaining momentum" at the power station, along with exploration of green hydrogen production.<ref>[https://www.tnb.com.my/assets/annual_report/TNB_IAR_2024.pdf Integrated Annual Report 2024], Tenaga Nasional Bhd, April 2025</ref>

In July 2025, TNB's Sustainability Report 2024 stated that a trial burn of empty fruit bunch (EFB) pellets was conducted at the power station.<ref>[https://www.tnb.com.my/assets/annual_report/TNB_Sustainability_Report_2024.pdf Sustainability Report 2024], Tenaga Nasional Bhd, July 2, 2025</ref>

In December 2025, TNB's "Sustainability Statement 2025" stated that "Project REACH", a green hydrogen production project, had been initiated at Jimah East power station. The venture would include a 500 kWp rooftop solar photovoltaic (PV) system and battery storage.<ref name=dec25/>

==Ownership==

Jimah East Power (JEP) is the sponsor of the project. TNB held a 70% stake in JEP while Mitsui & Co Ltd owned the remaining 30% through 3B Power. In July 2015, TNB said Chugoku Electric Power Co Inc, one of Japan’s biggest regional power utilities, might take up half of Mitsui's interest in 3B Power,<ref>[http://www.thestar.com.my/Business/Business-News/2015/07/09/New-shareholder-may-emerge-in-Project-3B-under-by-TNB-and-Mitsui/?style=biz "New shareholder may emerge in Project 3B under by TNB and Mitsui,"] The Star, July 9, 2015</ref> a deal announced in January 2016.<ref>[https://www.mitsui.com/jp/en/release/2016/1217087_8910.html "Partial Sale of Equity in 2,000MW Ultra Super Critical Coal-fired Power Project in Malaysia,"] Mitsui, January 20, 2016</ref>

In October 2021, Tenaga Nasional Berhad (TNB) was recognized as the "Clean Coal Technology Utilization for Large Power Generation" category winner at the ASEAN Energy Awards.<ref>[https://www.businesstoday.com.my/2021/10/10/tnb-jimah-plant-wins-asean-energy-award-for-clean-coal-technology/ "TNB Jimah Plant Wins ASEAN Energy Award For Clean Coal Technology,"] Business Today, October 10, 2021</ref> The month prior, TNB announced that the Jimah East power station would be the company's final coal endeavor.<ref>[https://www.tnb.com.my/assets/newsclip/11092021a.pdf "TNB's ambitious green energy plans,"] The Star, September 11, 2021</ref>

==Financing==

In November 2015, a financing agreement for this project was closed. HSBC, CIMB Group, and Maybank agreed to arrange US$2,065 million in bonds. Mitsui & Co and Tenaga Nasional agreed to provide US$610.53 million in equity. Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group, PwC, and HSBC acted as financial advisers.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://ijglobal.com/data/transaction/29438/jimah-east-coal-fired-power-plant-2000mw|title=Preview of Jimah East Coal Fired Power Plant (2000MW) {{!}} Transaction {{!}} IJGlobal|website=ijglobal.com|access-date=2020-11-16}}</ref>

==Environmental Degradation and Local Opposition==

A December 2021 narrative article discussed the environmental, social, and public health risks around coal-fired power production in Malaysia. One quote reads: "For Noh [a fishmonger in Chuah, Negeri Sembilan], the commissioning of the nearby Jimah Power Station in 2005 has made life much worse for him and the other fishers. Then a second plant, Jimah East Power Station, fired up in 2019. Since the power plants, fishing yields have crashed. When Noh started his trade in 1997, he worked with about 20 fishers. The yields then were high, with each fisher catching up to RM400 worth of fish a day, he recalls. But they can hardly haul up one-fourth of that now. The fishing community pulls in lighter and lighter nets, even empty ones. “We can no longer find prawns here,” says Noh." The article also mentions that the nearby seabed is now blackened and that crabs could no longer be found in the area either.<ref>[https://www.macaranga.org/coal-impact-fishermen-indigenous-malaysia/ "Coal Can Be Costly—Who's Paying?",] Macaranga, December 22, 2021</ref>

In 2023, it was reported that Jimah East Power Plant officials had offered monetary compensation to each local fishing boat in the amount of RM20,000, but the community of fisherpeople found the compensation a meager exchange for the damage inflicted on their homes, health, and livelihoods.<ref name=nofish23>[https://maritimefairtrade.org/too-little-and-very-late-screamed-kampung-chuah-against-environment-damage/ "Too Little And Very Late!” Screamed Kampung Chuah Against Environment Damage",] Maritime Fairtrade, March 16, 2023</ref> One local fisher said that the money was "nothing compared to the destruction of nature and depletion of fishing resources we live with in Kampung Chuah."<ref name=nofish23>[https://maritimefairtrade.org/too-little-and-very-late-screamed-kampung-chuah-against-environment-damage/ "Too Little And Very Late!” Screamed Kampung Chuah Against Environment Damage",] Maritime Fairtrade, March 16, 2023</ref>
